title: Markdown to knowledge graph, in your browser
description: edgextract's approach in one tab: an ontology (one of 27 curated domains or 13 of Neo4j's solution packages, each with synthetic documents written in its field's genre, or your own Ontology Graph Spec 1.1 document, read with the official SDK) decides which kinds, links and property values are legal, GLiNER2.5 (through gliner-rs, compiled to WebAssembly) scores every candidate, and cutoffs you own sort each answer into keep, review or drop. Relate 1.3.0, compiled to WebAssembly and kept in this site's private storage (OPFS), holds the ontology and its engine-enforced graph type, the inference cache, the review queue and the knowledge graph; a Cypher console queries it read-only, NVL draws it, and the database downloads as a snapshot that native Relate opens.
summary: Turn a markdown document into a knowledge graph in your browser tab. An ontology says what is legal, GLiNER2.5 scores every candidate, you set the cutoffs, and Relate keeps the graph in the browser's own storage.
browser: Needs a current Chromium-based desktop browser (module workers, OPFS with sync access handles in a worker, WebAssembly) and about 1 GB of free site storage: the first visit downloads the 304 MB GLiNER2.5-small model from the Hugging Face Hub and caches it.
credits: Relate 1.3.0 WebAssembly build (Apache-2.0), served here as a pinned copy of npm's @relate/relate-wasm 1.3.0.
NVL 2.0.0, the Neo4j Visualization Library (proprietary), used with Neo4j's permission (confirmed by the repository owner on 2026-10-08).

Neo4j's solution packages from studio-agent-use-cases (b76f767), used with Neo4j's permission (confirmed by the repository owner on 2026-11-26); those drawn from the EDM Council's FIBO carry its MIT notices.

create-context-graph (neo4j-labs/create-context-graph, Apache-2.0): its POLE+O base, for a create-context-graph file pasted into the editor, and the list of domains the curated ontologies follow; the documents were written for this page and are synthetic (their people, organisations and identifiers fictional, their places real).
